recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source edit is needed for FHIR-11333 unless a future Patient Care decision intentionally changes CarePlan.encounter semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-11333 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request against DSTU2 CarePlan.context asking that the definition stop saying the care plan was defined in a context and instead clarify the original context in which the CarePlan was created.
initial_application: Commit f39dde8e171836d3345715f788c746e0a1624492 explicitly applied #11333 by changing the then-authoritative CarePlan.context spreadsheet definition from "Identifies the context in which this particular CarePlan is defined" to "Identifies the original context in which this particular CarePlan was created."
additional_context: CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini. Later workflow alignment renamed CarePlan.context to CarePlan.encounter and narrowed the target to Encounter, while preserving the creation-context meaning as "The Encounter during which this CarePlan was created or to which the creation of this record is tightly associated." FHIR-11171 later relied on this clarification when deciding that CarePlan.context could still support longitudinal care plans and separately clarified CarePlan.period. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source describes the encounter associated with CarePlan record creation, not a boundary that confines all care plan activity to that encounter, and the comment explicitly says resulting activities may occur in other encounters.

related_jiras.note: Later Published CarePlan clarification that cites FHIR-11333 and confirms the context wording does not prevent longitudinal care plans.
